audit_findings.title: The bridge treats all cash and short-term investments as distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $170.12 million added to equity value, equal to $2.98 per share and 31.4% of base-case equity value; $95.0 million was subsequently used to repay the revolver
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash and short-term investments to equity value without reserving operating cash; because debt principal is not deducted, cash subsequently used to repay debt cannot also remain in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on past performance and current expectations, we believe that our cash flows from operations, cash on hand and investments will satisfy our working capital needs, capital expenditures, commitments and other liquidity requirements associated with our existing operations, as well as announced growth, diversification and optimization initiatives through the next fiscal year and beyond.
audit_findings.explanation: The full-surplus treatment is demonstrably aggressive and materially affects every scenario. The exact excess-cash correction remains unresolved, but the filed $95.0 million post-quarter debt repayment shows that a substantial portion of the June liquidity was not still available for distribution. The later release of the $19.6 million letter of credit removes that particular restriction but does not establish that the remaining liquidity is surplus.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct cash, investments, revolver debt and restricted liquidity as of the valuation date; determine minimum operating and committed-growth cash; rerun all scenarios adding only excess cash and consistently reflect the related change in interest expense.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved borrower-defense recoupment may rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any successful ED recoupment would create a cash liability ahead of common equity and could also reduce future owner earnings through legal, compliance or financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: If ED were to discharge some amount of loans, ED will, at a later date, determine whether to engage in a separate proceeding to recoup such amount from the applicable school.
audit_findings.explanation: The approximately 2,500 claims and possible recoupment process are filed facts, but no discharged-loan amount, probability, accrual, indemnification recovery or insurance recovery is supplied. This is therefore an unresolved contingent exposure, not a demonstrated valuation error, and the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the aggregate loan principal associated with the claims, adjudication status, recoupment defenses, purchase-agreement indemnities, insurance coverage and recorded accruals; probability-weight any uncovered exposure and rerun the equity bridge.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings depends on a highly judgmental student-loan collection estimate
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.146 million of notes receivable at June 30, 2026 and $22.403 million of nine-month credit-loss provision; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The collection estimate affects recognized tuition revenue, credit-loss expense, receivable cash conversion and therefore the sustainable owner-earnings anchor and terminal earnings base.
audit_findings.evidence: Estimating the collection rate requires significant management judgment.
audit_findings.explanation: Management judgment is demonstrated and the collection-rate estimate was identified as a critical audit matter, but the supplied record contains no alternative collection-rate sensitivity or cohort cash realization data. It therefore does not demonstrate that the estimate is optimistic. The exposure may be material because the note balance is about 197% of the $26.5 million anchor and collection assumptions can affect recurring earnings, but the valuation effect cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each loan cohort's recognized revenue to collections, defaults, recoveries and write-offs; obtain the auditor or management sensitivity to alternative lookback periods; rerun the anchor and terminal value using supportable stressed collection rates.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require reinvestment beyond that embedded in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.9 million of capital expenditures and $27.6 million of disclosed strategic-growth expenses during the nine months ended June 30, 2026, respectively 305% and 104% of the $26.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Required campus and program capital expenditures, working capital, lease costs, pre-opening expenses and ramp losses reduce owner earnings generated by the assumed growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Pending regulatory approval, we expect to launch a minimum of six programs annually at our existing campuses and open at least two new campuses each year between fiscal years 2026 and 2029, thus expanding both UTI’s and Concorde’s campus offerings and footprint.
audit_findings.explanation: This is more than a remote future possibility: filed 2026 results already show substantial growth spending while the valuation mechanically grows the FY2025 anchor. Those costs may produce later returns, so they should not automatically be treated as permanent expenses, but the disclosed scale is large enough to change the operating valuation materially if the scenarios omit the reinvestment required to achieve growth.
audit_findings.action: Build campus- and program-level growth schedules covering capital expenditures, working capital, lease payments, pre-opening costs, ramp losses and mature returns; rerun bear, base and bull owner earnings with those cash outlays explicitly matched to their growth assumptions.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may contain a nonrecurring stock-compensation tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.851 million, equal to 10.8% of the anchor; if entirely removed, computed base value falls about $40.0 million or $0.70 per share, from $9.49 to approximately $8.79
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit would inflate the owner-earnings anchor and every projected year's earnings while retained stock-compensation expense remains an operating cost.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective income tax rate for the year ended September 30, 2025 differed from the federal statutory tax rate of 21% primarily due to non-deductible executive compensation, stock compensation, refinements to the federal research and development tax credits, and state and local income and franchise taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing shows the $2.851 million tax-reconciliation benefit, but does not establish that it is wholly nonrecurring or that the owner-earnings calculation failed to normalize it. Even treating the entire amount as an erroneous recurring benefit reduces estimated base value by about 7.4%; the adjusted base value remains far below the $22.20 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $2.851 million tax-reconciliation item into the owner-earnings calculation and separate ordinary tax deductions from excess exercise or settlement benefits; document the normalization, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated by the supplied upper-bound scale.

audit_findings.title: Surety-bond reimbursement exposure is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.9 million latest filed face amount; a full uncompensated draw would equal $0.51 per share and 5.3% of base-case equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A bond draw would create a reimbursement liability ahead of common equity, reduced by any existing accrual, collateral or restricted cash attributable to the bonds.
audit_findings.evidence: We are obligated to reimburse our insurers for any surety bonds that are paid by the insurers.
audit_findings.explanation: The reimbursement obligation exists, but no draw or probable loss is demonstrated. Even the conservative assumption that the entire latest $28.9 million face amount becomes an uncovered claim would reduce base value from $9.49 to approximately $8.98 per share, still far below the $22.20 market price. The actual incremental exposure should be lower to the extent bonds are undrawn or collateralized.
audit_findings.action: Confirm outstanding bond amounts, compliance status, historical draws, insurer collateral, related restricted cash and any accrual; monitor for a probable draw and reopen the bridge only if uncovered exposure rises materially beyond the current filed face amount.
